chunks: Al-Tawhid: My father, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
His Chair extends over the Heavens and the Earth
He said: The Heavens, the Earth, and what is between them are in the Chair, and the Throne is the Knowledge whom no one can estimate its limit.

key_terms.كُرْسِيُّهُ: His Chair (a symbol of divine power or containment)
key_terms.وَالْعَرْشُ: And the Throne (often associated with divine knowledge or authority)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Kursi and the Arsh according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kulayni’s chain, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a metaphysical interpretation of Ayat al-Kursi, identifying the 'Kursi' (Chair) as the container of the physical cosmos and the 'Arsh' (Throne) as the domain of Divine Knowledge. This aligns with the Shia scholarly tradition of distinguishing between the created universe and the uncreated, infinite knowledge of Allah, emphasizing that while the physical realm is vast, it is still contained within the greater reality of God's knowledge, which surpasses all comprehension.

en.ammaar-muslim: 6. [6/343] al-Tawhid: My father from Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abdallah b. Sinan from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام about the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: “
His Chair extends over the Heavens and the Earth” [2:255] -
He said: The Heavens, the Earth and what is between them is within the Chair while the Throne (Arsh) is the Knowledge whom no one can estimate its limit.
